title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
summary: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
summary: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
summary: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
summary: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.

title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
summary: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

title: Occupancy Driven Phase Transitions in Gapped Systems
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to Phys. Rev. Lett
summary: Systems characterized by an energy gap between the ground state and excited states support a growing number of thermal excitations upon raising the temperature. Provided these excitations interact with each other, their number affects the size of the energy gap akin to a harmonic oscillator where the oscillation frequency is damping dependent. Here we show that once a critical number of excitations is reached, the excitation population becomes thermodynamically unstable and the system transitions between two states. This transition is marked by a divergence in the specific heat, which does not have to be accompanied by an order parameter, nor by the full closure of the gap. We illustrate the thermodynamics using a simple two level system and superfluid $^4$He as examples, and we argue that the hidden order transition in URu$_2$Si$_2$ is an example of such an occupancy driven transition in the absence of an order parameter.

title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
summary: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.

title: Discrete time liquids
comment: 8 pages main + 9 pages supplement, 4 figures main + 10 figures supplement
summary: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.

title: Stochastic Diversity Stabilization in Nonlinear Competitive Dynamics: A Statistical Mechanics Approach to Fluctuation Suppression and Finite-Size Scaling
comment: 38 pages, 8 figures (including supplementary material). Accepted manuscript of the article published in Physica A 701 (2026) 132041
summary: Stochastic forcing can prevent diversity collapse in competitive dynamical systems, yet the quantitative conditions and the dynamical mechanism responsible remain poorly characterized. We address both questions in a class of nonlinear stochastic replicator dynamics on the N-dimensional probability simplex, parameterized by a nonlinearity exponent gamma and additive Gaussian noise of intensity sigma. Under the baseline interaction, the minimum noise required to sustain diversity decays as a power law, sigma_c ~ N^(-alpha); replacing the baseline interaction with a superlinear variant shifts alpha from about 1.1 to about 2.0, in agreement with a linear-stability prediction alpha = (gamma+2)/2, identifying alpha as a model-specific quantity rather than a universal index. Scanning the (gamma, sigma) plane reveals a smooth dynamical crossover: the fluctuation susceptibility chi_H = N Var(H) peaks at gamma ~ 0.7 (chi_H ~ 0.6) and is suppressed at high gamma, with no divergence near gamma ~ 1.4; matched finite-size analysis finds no systematic divergence of the peak with N, ruling out a genuine second-order phase transition. The entropy relaxation time tau_relax(gamma) remains approximately constant (about 2.9 time units) across the full range of gamma, even as chi_H decreases sixfold; this decoupling between relaxation timescale and fluctuation amplitude implies that suppression arises from convergence of diverse pathways to similar endpoints rather than from accelerated relaxation along a single channel. These findings identify nonlinear fluctuation suppression via pathway multiplicity -- distinct from both noise-induced transitions and equilibrium criticality -- as the operative stabilization pattern in this class of nonequilibrium stochastic systems.

title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
summary: Donor substitution can tune the coupled ferroelectric, dielectric, electronic, and optical properties of perovskite oxides by modifying lattice distortions and electronic screening. We investigate these effects in La-doped BaTiO3 using density functional theory, density-functional perturbation theory, and the Berry-phase formalism for polarization. For a model with 12.5% La substitution at the Ba site, La incorporation induces anisotropic lattice contraction, reduces tetragonality and Ti off-centering, and weakens the energetic stabilization of the tetragonal ferroelectric phase. The accompanying reduction in polarization is associated with enhanced electronic screening and reduced anomalous Born effective charges. Phonon calculations indicate that the relaxed doped structure is dynamically stable, while hardening of a low-frequency polar mode is consistent with weakened ferroelectricity. The high-frequency dielectric response increases moderately, whereas the static dielectric response decreases as the lattice contribution is suppressed. Electronic-structure calculations show a Fermi-level shift toward the conduction band without mid-gap defect states. The optical spectra exhibit an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein-Moss-type mechanism, enhanced near-edge transparency, and reduced birefringence. Together, these results suggest a microscopic connection between donor-induced screening, polar-mode hardening, reduced dynamical charges, polarization suppression, and decreased optical anisotropy. The conclusions apply to the investigated 12.5% composition; calculations at additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.

title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
summary: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

title: First-order differential constraints for the nonlinear wave equation:wave fronts, admissible nonlinearities and exact solutions
summary: We construct exact solutions of the nonlinear wave equation in three space dimensions by the method of linear determining equations: first-order constraint functions are found as solutions of the linear determining equation, the differential constraints obtained by setting them equal to zero are integrated, and the resulting ansatz is substituted into the equation. Lie point symmetries are a special case, and the solutions obtained generically have no symmetry. The determining equations tie the admissible nonlinearity to the geometry of the constraint: arbitrary on characteristic hyperplanes, cubic on light cones, and, for a pair of constraints, exponential on light cones and quintic on the cylindrical fronts of a line source. Among the solutions are smooth bounded sine-Gordon walls and vortex configurations whose shape varies arbitrarily along a front, the fields of point sources moving on arbitrary trajectories for the cubic and Liouville equations, with an exact nonlinear analogue of the Larmor formula for the power radiated in the cubic case, and smooth finite-energy solutions of the cubic equation with any prescribed number of toroidal nodal surfaces.

title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
summary: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by ${}_S\langle Ψ| \hatψ(x)\hatψ(x') | Ψ\rangle_S$, where $|Ψ\rangle_S$ is the superconducting state, and where $\hatψ(x)$ is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al.\ regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J.\ Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

title: Nonlinear Canonical Transformations for Studying Spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
comment: Accepted for publication in The Journal of Chemical Physics
summary: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ spin models provide demanding benchmarks. Spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. We introduce a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian into a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions, as nonlocal strings can appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.

title: Charge-monitored Luttinger liquid
summary: We discuss phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids without particle number conservation, such as those in proximity to a superconductor, subjected to weak continuous measurements of their particle density, in the regime where the bosonization approach is applicable. We show that the phases of these systems are controlled by the competition between measurements, which favor the area-law phase and particle tunneling in and out of the Luttinger liquid, which favors the volume-law phase. The volume-law phase in this system is always charge fuzzy. We show that within this framework, the phase boundary between the two phases is given by a universal dependence of the Luttinger parameter on the measurement rate. This behavior can be contrasted with the non-universal phase boundaries in more generic highly excited one dimensional systems whose behavior is no longer captured by the Luttinger liquid framework.

title: Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices
summary: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

title: Resonant-pair energy return beyond the early Green-Kubo plateau in a quartic chain
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables; includes supplementary material and machine-readable source data
summary: Distinguishing rapid local energy exchange from sustained transport matters when thermal conductivity is inferred from finite simulations. In a weakly coupled chain of separable quartic oscillators, we identify a quantitative mechanism that changes an early Green--Kubo plateau: resonant neighbors exchange energy and coherently return it. The pair heat-current integral maps to the classical pendulum trapping response. Quartic homogeneity gives an energy-independent reference period $T_{\rm lib}=7.77ε^{-1/2}$, where $ε$ is the coupling. Without fitted parameters, the leading response predicts a negative first minimum at $0.952T_{\rm lib}$ with depth $-0.74$ times the independent-cell exchange coefficient. Isolated-pair simulations test this reference and resolve finite-coupling corrections. The chain reaches its first minimum on the same time scale, with a shallower minimum and a small later residual. Comparisons with chaotic cells and energy-conserving noise show regimes in which coherent return is absent or interrupted over the measured windows. These finite-time results provide a quantitative reference for separating the early exchange plateau from subsequent correlated dynamics.

title: Domain walls in $R3c$-structured NaNbO$_3$
summary: In this work, we undertake a systematic first-principles study of structural domain walls in the low-temperature rhombohedral $R3c$ phase of perovskite oxide NaNbO$_3$. Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the $R3c$ structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and charge neutrality, and perform structural relaxations for each representative domain wall class. We find that one class of 109° domain walls has a notably low energy of 9 mJ m$^{-2}$, comparable to the low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO$_3$. Finally, we find that this class of 109° walls is compatible with the crystal twinning observed in experiments on the $R3c$ phase, and propose an atomistic mechanism for the $R3c \leftrightarrow Pbcm$ phase transition.

title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.

title: A sharp gradient-corrected Lieb--Thirring inequality in one dimension with applications to density functional theory
summary:
We first prove a sharp Lieb-Thirring inequality with semi-classical constant and gradient correction in one dimension. In the periodic setting, the corresponding inequality also includes a parity dependent shell-correction term, which appears to be new. Moreover, we also characterize the optimizers of these inequalities. In particular, the optimizing density profiles form a two-dimensional manifold, which we call here the Poincaré density manifold.
  We then apply these results to study the Thomas--Fermi--von Weizsäcker (TFW) approximation of the kinetic energy in Density Functional Theory. More precisely, we first obtain an explicit and non-asymptotic bound on the global and local error made by the TFW approximation. These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincaré density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincaré manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincaré manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit $N \rightarrow \infty$ with asymptotic rate of order $N^{-2}$. This rate is shown to be optimal.

title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
summary: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca$_2$CuO$_2$Cl$_2$, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic $4a_0 \times 2a_0$ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed $4a_0$ electronic structures.

title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
summary: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
summary: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size $N$, which goes from $\mathcal{O}({\rm poly}(N))$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.

title: $π$-Flux Tuning of Quantum Paramagnetism in the Triangular-Lattice Hubbard Model
summary: We compare two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models at half filling: the zero-flux model and a staggered $π$-flux model with zero and $π$ flux through oppositely oriented triangles. Although both reduce to the same Heisenberg model at leading order in the strong-coupling limit, their distinct charge fluctuation profiles yield different quantum paramagnetic regimes. Combining a strong-coupling expansion with infinite density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) calculations, we find that the positive ring-exchange of the zero-flux model promotes spontaneous chirality, consistent with its notion of a chiral spin liquid at intermediate coupling. In the staggered-$π$-flux model, whose noninteracting limit is a Dirac semimetal, the ring exchange changes sign and disfavors chiral order and we find no resolvable scalar chirality. This renders flux-tuned ring-exchange an efficient discriminator between chiral and non-chiral quantum paramagnets at finite coupling.

title: Foresight-dependent entropy production in stochastic two-agent dynamics
summary: Nonreciprocal interactions can break detailed balance by sustaining stationary probability currents. Here we ask whether such currents can also emerge when the agents' immediate coordination preferences are reciprocal, but their state-adjustment rules are determined by forward-looking optimization (foresight). We study a minimal stochastic linear-quadratic game in which two agents control noisy scalar states and minimize individual discounted costs in a full-information feedback Nash equilibrium. The optimized controls yield an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process whose stationary probability current and entropy-production rate, measuring statistical time-irreversibility, can be calculated exactly. For reciprocal coordination with unequal self-anchoring strengths, the effective drift asymmetry first appears at order $τ^5$, where $τ$ is the planning timescale, and the normalized entropy production consequently scales as $τ^8$ in the limit $τ\to0$. We derive this cancellation from the coupled Nash Riccati equations. For conformist-contrarian coupling, normalized entropy production approaches a nonzero short-foresight limit and initially decreases from that limit by an amount proportional to $τ^2$. We also determine the long-foresight limit for a conformist-contrarian pair with equal self-anchoring strengths. Numerical solutions of the full Nash equations verify the asymptotic laws and reveal the effect of foresight. Thus, forward-looking optimization can generate or reduce normalized stationary irreversibility, depending on the underlying interaction.

title: Peridynamic Thermo-Mechanical Modeling of Cracking in Tungsten under Fusion-Relevant Heat Fluxes
summary: Plasma-facing materials (PFMs) are the primary armor materials in fusion reactors, protecting reactor wall components from extreme heat fluxes, energetic particles, and intense neutron irradiation. These harsh conditions induce thermo-mechanical stresses, irradiation damage, and overall degradation in PFMs. Among these, thermo-mechanical damage induced by extreme heat flux is one of the key factors limiting the lifetime of PFMs. We present a modeling and simulation approach for predicting thermo-mechanical cracking and damage in tungsten, a leading PFM candidate, under fusion-reactor-relevant heat fluxes. Specifically, we study damage induced by cyclic electron beam (e-beam) exposure under different combinations of base temperature and heat flux. We carry out component-scale thermo-mechanical simulations using CabanaPD, a peridynamics fracture mechanics code, informed by experimental data for recrystallized pure tungsten from the JUDITH e-beam facility. The simulations compare well with the experimental classification and enable identification of cracking thresholds across a range of heat fluxes and base temperatures. These predictions can provide detailed insights into the spatial distribution and temporal accumulation of cracks and damage, while offering a pathway for screening candidate PFMs and quantifying their lifespan under fusion-relevant conditions.

title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

title: Dirac Structures and Reduction of Optimal Control Problems with Symmetries
summary: We study the symmetry reduction of optimal control problems using Dirac structures. The first-order conditions of the Pontryagin Maximum Principle are written as an implicit Dirac system on the Pontryagin bundle. For a problem invariant under a Lie group, we reduce both the Lagrange-Pontryagin variational principle and the underlying Dirac structure, and prove that they yield the same reduced equations, which we identify with the Hamiltonian equations on the dual of the Atiyah algebroid. Reconstruction, independence of the principal connection, and the relation between criticality and optimality complete the picture. Dropping regularity, we give the Gotay-Nester-Hinds constraint algorithm a Dirac-geometric form and prove that symmetry reduction commutes with it. For control-linear systems whose admissible directions are horizontal for a principal connection, abnormal extremals lie on the leaf where the base costate vanishes, and the first secondary constraint is the degeneracy of the curvature pairing. We also give a reduced criterion for strict abnormality and a metric-free index form. Examples: a spacecraft with rotors (flat connection), the Heisenberg group (nowhere-zero curvature) and the Martinet problem (curvature vanishing on a hypersurface).

title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
summary: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+δ^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

title: Symmetry-Preserving Local Representation for Short-Range Interaction in Complex Materials
summary: Modeling short-range interactions in highly disordered materials remains challenging due to the immense configuration space and the disruption of local symmetry in truncated theoretical models. Here, we propose a symmetry-preserving local representation framework that strictly enforces topological continuity and translational invariance via boundary passivation. Applied to high-entropy alloys, this approach autonomously unravels the nonlinear ligand effects modulating local reactivity and accurately captures coverage-dependent many-body interactions without explicit periodic expansion. By resolving the conflict between localized chemical environments and extended periodic boundaries, this framework not only reduces computational complexity by an order of magnitude but also provides a physically transparent paradigm for deciphering short-range order in complex condensed matter systems.

title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
summary: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

title: Einstein's theory of Brownian motion: The non-Fickian normal diffusion
summary: Einstein's theory of diffusion defines what is considered {\it normal diffusion}. Historically, Einstein considered homogeneous diffusion characterised by a diffusion constant in his original calculations, resulting in what is known as {\it Fickian} diffusion, which thermally relaxes concentration inhomogeneities. However, in the same derivation of Einstein, the seed of generalisation of the theory to {\it non-Fickian} diffusion in the presence of space-dependent diffusivity is hidden. This indicates that non-Fickian diffusion, which can drive concentration inhomogeneities, can also be normal diffusion. The present article discusses the origin of the {\it normal} non-Fickian diffusion in Einstein's theory of diffusion.

title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
summary: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) offers substantial advantages to the fabrication of complex structural components, but its widespread adoption is slowed due to complexities in the process-structure-property relations which is the cause for uncertainty and drives risk. Accurately quantifying these complex relations solely via experimental workflows is time consuming and costly. Integrated computational materials and engineering (ICME) frameworks address this challenge by leveraging advanced computational tools, such as crystal plasticity finite element models (CPFEM), to predict critical mechanical properties directly from microstructural data. However, these frameworks require a large datasets that are often difficult to obtain, and their predictive accuracy depends on the availability of realistic AM microstructure representations. Additionally, we establish a classifier-free guidance framework for solving complex inverse problems such as property-to-structure and process-to-structure mappings, and we showcase a potential application on a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification problem. title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
summary: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.

title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
summary: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
summary: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This generates additional low-$Q$ components and enhances the Auger coupling by more than five orders of magnitude relative to pristine GaN. Thus, we provide a microscopic explanation for the competing trends in radiative and Auger recombination. More broadly, our results establish localization contrast as a mechanism through which disorder can control optical and carrier-carrier interactions in semiconductors.

title: Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts
summary: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices, with $(n,m) = (1,1), (2,2)$ and $(2,4)$, from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts. The resulting $C$-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with $a^-b^+c^-$ or $a^-b^-c^-$ octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a $d$-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. Within DFT+U, the splitting reaches 118 meV in the insulating (LVO)$_1$/(LNO)$_1$ superlattice, about twice that calculated for bulk LaVO$_3$, and decreases as the nickelate layers become thicker. Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen $2p$ states through $p$-$d$ covalency. Interfacial charge transfer thus emerges as a \textit{design} principle for engineering altermagnetism in oxide heterostructures.

title: Hierarchical Reduction of Invariant Subspaces: From Fragmentation to Many-Body Scars
summary: We investigate a hierarchy of invariant Hilbert-space structures connecting Hilbert-space fragmentation, partial solvability, and quantum many-body scars. For spin chains with fragmented spin-$1/2$ subspaces and their local deformations, we show, using the spin-$1$ $XXC$ chain as a representative example, how successive local deformations reduce extensive irreducible-string fragmentation through an implicitly embedded spin-$1/2$ invariant space and ultimately to a single scar tower, connecting the $XXC$, perturbed $XXC$, and spin-$1$ $XY$ scar models. We also establish a rigidity constraint on isolating nonsymmetric towers and a constructive correspondence that transfers a reduction between locally realizable representations of the embedded dynamics. The latter demonstrates that the reduction hierarchy can be transferred through a unitary transformation within the embedded subspace, yielding an exact scar tower built on a Néel reference state without requiring unitary equivalence of the full Hamiltonians.

title: Design of Nuclear and Magnetic Scattering Length Density Profiles
summary: The scattering length density (SLD) profile of a sample can be deliberately designed to enhance the information of interest obtained from neutron reflectometry. Here, we demonstrate this approach using amorphous $\mathrm{Fe}_{x}\mathrm{Co}_{y}\mathrm{Al}_{8}\mathrm{Zr}_{2}$ thin films. Four samples, each comprising ten repetitions of an AlZr spacer layer and a magnetic layer, were prepared with magnetic-layer compositions of $\mathrm{Fe}_{80}\mathrm{Co}_{10}\mathrm{Al}_{8}\mathrm{Zr}_{2}$, $\mathrm{Fe}_{70}\mathrm{Co}_{20}\mathrm{Al}_{8}\mathrm{Zr}_{2}$, $\mathrm{Fe}_{60}\mathrm{Co}_{30}\mathrm{Al}_{8}\mathrm{Zr}_{2}$, and $\mathrm{Fe}_{45}\mathrm{Co}_{45}\mathrm{Al}_{8}\mathrm{Zr}_{2}$, and characterised using X-ray and polarised neutron reflectometry. Across the series, the nuclear SLD of the FeCoAlZr alloy decreases approximately linearly from $7.14 \times 10^{-6}$ to $4.63 \times 10^{-6}$ $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-2}$ with increasing Co content, while the magnetic SLD is approximately $4.3$-$4.5 \times 10^{-6}$ $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}^{-2}$. title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
comment: 81 pages, 34 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook in the ancillary files
summary: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. title: Symmetric and antisymmetric cumulant hierarchies and Wick polynomials of operators
summary: There has been much progress in understanding mathematical foundations of kinetic theory in recent years, in particular, for the original model of a rarefied gas of classical particles with repulsive interactions, as well as for weakly nonlinear wave evolutions related to wave turbulence. As an application, we derive a hierarchy of evolution equations satisfied by such cumulants, usually called truncated correlation functions in this context, for a gas of bosons or fermions hopping on a finite lattice and interacting via a two-body potential. With sufficient control over solutions to these hierarchies, one could control the magnitude of the error terms related to an approximation of the state of the quantum system by a finite lattice kinetic equation studied in our earlier work, closely connected to standard bosonic and fermionic Boltzmann--Nordheim equations.

title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
summary: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.

title: Unrestricted Binary Tree State for the Fermionic Hubbard Model
comment: Submitted to Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics
summary: Binary tree states have been introduced as compact correlated pair wave functions that improve upon the antisymmetrized geminal power by adding variational flexibility. Here, we extend the binary tree state to the fermionic half-filled Hubbard model using restricted and unrestricted orbitals. Although the ansatz is seniority zero in its optimized pairing basis, its expansion in the original Hubbard site basis can contain nonzero site- seniority character, while unrestricted orbital optimization provides additional flexibility through independent spin-up and spin-down orbitals. This provides a mechanism for a paired ansatz to describe the singly occupied configurations that dominate the repulsive Hubbard model at large U/t. We find that unrestricted BTS closely approaches optimized DOCI in the repulsive regime, substantially improves upon AGP, and reproduces DOCI density correlations more accurately than pCCD

title: Learning Cole-Hopf Coordinates for Stochastic Growth Dynamics: the KPZ class
summary:
Inferring effective equations from observations of nonlinear stochastic processes is challenging because individual trajectories are noisy realizations, while the relevant physical information is encoded in ensemble statistics. We introduce a data-driven framework that learns a change of variables in which nonlinear stochastic dynamics become linear. The model combines a neural change of representation with a linear stochastic latent evolution and is trained through a short-time moment-matching objective, thereby avoiding trajectory \rev{simulation} during optimization. This construction yields an interpretable generative model: both the learned transformation and the latent evolution operators can be directly inspected.
  We validate the method on the one-dimensional Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation, a paradigmatic model of stochastic growth for which the Cole--Hopf transformation maps the nonlinear dynamics to the stochastic heat equation. From simulated height trajectories alone, the model recovers the local exponential Cole--Hopf map and the associated linear stochastic operator. Generated trajectories reproduce the main statistical signatures of the KPZ universality class, including the growth law $\mathrm{Var}(h^{t})\sim t^{2β}$ with $β=1/3$ and the GOE Tracy--Widom height distribution for flat initial conditions. These results show that interpretable stochastic equations can be inferred from data by learning representations in which the dynamics closes in a simple form. Furthermore the development of the physical informed learning permits to get insights on the physics of the dynamical process.

title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
summary: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base $γ$/$γ^{\prime}$ strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~$^{\circ}$C in \SI{100}{\hour}, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.

title: From bulk flows to boundary generators and costs
summary: Holographic complexity admits a broad family of bulk observables, yet their relation to boundary state-preparation costs remains unclear. We propose a local prescription that associates suitable bulk observables with quadratic cost geometries on families of states prepared by Euclidean sources. Building on the holographic transport of bulk Hamiltonian flows to Euclidean preparation sources, we use the Hessian of the transported generator at a stationary reference state to define a candidate cost metric. When this Hessian is positive definite, the minimised preparation energy reproduces the change in the bulk observable to quadratic order. We characterise the resulting preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and compute them for the maximal volume in scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$. At large-conformal dimension, we recover the known proportionality between cost and Fubini-Study metrics. At finite dimension, we obtain positive but generally unequal penalties for source variations that displace the bulk field and its conjugate momentum, breaking this proportionality even for a single scalar operator. We further study a deformation of volume by quadratic scalar and gradient terms in the large-dimension regime, determining how the couplings modify the penalties and constrain positivity. These additions selectively change field-displacement costs, with the gradient term introducing mode dependence. Our results provide an explicit local connection between the choice of bulk observables and the assignment of boundary preparation penalties.

title: An elliptic generalization of the $D^{(2)}_{2}$ Spin chain
summary: An integrable elliptic generalization of the closed $D^{(2)}_2$ quantum spin chain is constructed. Taking the trigonometric limit, we have shown that the corresponding R-matrix reduces to that of the $D^{(2)}_2$ one, up to a similarity transformation. Basing on the very fact of the factorization for the R-matrix and the corresponding transfer matrix which indeed ensures the integrability of the model, we give the exact solution of the model which can be expressed in terms of a homogeneous T-Q relation.

title: Site and bond percolation thresholds of all $k$-uniform tilings with $k\le 10$
comment: 19 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Code, data and raw histograms: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23533708
summary: We determine the site and bond percolation thresholds of all 23,396 $k$-uniform tilings of the plane by regular polygons with $k\le 10$, the complete set according to the known enumeration. We use Monte Carlo simulation on tori and the condition that no wrapping and a cross-wrapping cluster are equally probable, the Monte Carlo form of the critical-polynomial criterion, which needs no knowledge of the large-scale anisotropy that most of these lattices have. The 486 thresholds with $k\le4$ have uncertainties of a few units in the sixth decimal and reproduce the 22 Archimedean reference values (rms deviation 0.71 standard errors) and unpublished bond thresholds of the 20 two-uniform lattices ($χ^2=19.5$ for 20 values); the others have median statistical uncertainties of $2\times10^{-5}$ ($k\le7$) to $7\times10^{-5}$ ($k\ge8$) and no detectable finite-size bias. The vertex-type fractions alone fix the thresholds for $k\ge5$ to about $2\times10^{-3}$ (linear rule fitted on $k\le4$), while tilings with equal composition differ by up to $6\times10^{-3}$ (site) and $2\times10^{-2}$ (bond). In the range of domain sizes covered, descriptors of radius one account for more than half of this difference, and stackings of identical strips have thresholds linear in the fraction of each boundary type. For tilings that differ only by the registry of strips separated by $h$ rows of squares, the bond threshold difference decreases by a factor of 6-8 per row, comparable to the leading momentum-$π$ eigenvalue of the square-band transfer matrix.

title: Nonlinear Canonical Transformations for Studying Spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
comment: Accepted for publication in The Journal of Chemical Physics
summary: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ spin models provide demanding benchmarks. Spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. We introduce a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian into a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions, as nonlocal strings can appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.

title: Active phase separation from concentration-dependent diffusion in chemical networks
summary: Active phase separation in living systems is ubiquitous, yet the microscopic origins of the non-equilibrium terms in active field theories remain largely unknown. Here, starting from stochastic mass-conserving reaction-diffusion dynamics of two interacting chemical species, we perform a systematic slow-mode reduction and derive the complete Active Model B+ field theory, with all phenomenological coefficients expressed in terms of microscopic parameters. We identify concentration-dependent diffusivities and asymmetric inter-species chemotactic couplings as the minimal microscopic ingredients generating the genuinely non-equilibrium coefficient responsible for microphase separation, cluster phases, and arrested coarsening. Our framework recovers the equilibrium limit consistently and is validated by stochastic numerical simulations. These results establish a direct, bottom-up link between the architecture of chemical reaction networks and the universality class of their emergent large-scale dynamics.

title: Decoding Composition-Structure-Performance Relations in Sodium Layered Oxide Positive Electrode Materials
summary: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na$_x$TMO$_2$, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds. We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na$_x$TM$_{0.5}$TM$'_{0.5}$O$_2$ oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO$_6$ octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn$^{3+}$ and Ni$^{3+}$ through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers. We formulate an energy-density-versus-strain map that yields a design rule: a high-voltage couple without Jahn--Teller strain, which Mn$^{4+}$/Ni$^{2+}$ charge transfer realizes in Na$_x$Mn$_{0.5}$Ni$_{0.5}$O$_2$, the most practical composition. We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.

title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
summary: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

title: Some minimal characteristics and flat trajectories of a system in the N-body problem
summary: For the classical model of a system of N particles with interaction (the N-body problem) we consider some spatial problems of nonlinear programming for finding conditional minima and local extrema for the main characteristics of the system on its phase space. We prove that these conditional minima and local extrema of the system characteristics can only be achieved on flat, in general, not necessarily finite, trajectories of the system in space, (under the condition that the system angular momentum is non-zero). And then we find the basic conditions limiting the values of the integrals of motion: angular momentum and total energy of the system under which these trajectories are flat finite ("circular" or elliptical) trajectories on which the flat structure of the system is preserved in time under the certain restrictions on the values of the system's integrals of motion. And we determine also the values of the system's key characteristics on these flat trajectories. Next, in the Appendix, we consider some additional related results for a more general model of the system.

summary: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The examination of electronic structure indicates that, in contrast to the conventional h-BN, which is an insulator with the wide band gap, the predicted orthorhombic phase is expected to be a semiconductor with the narrow band gap of ~ 0.65 eV.

title: Big Crunching Your Big Bang: Doubly Warped Time-Dependent Type II Flux Backgrounds and Scale Separation
summary: We construct three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions of massless type IIA supergravity with different choices of fluxes, namely, $H_3$, $\tilde F_2$ and $\tilde F_4$ along internal directions. The $H_3$ solution also belongs to the common NS--NS sector of type IIB. Our solutions show that, without localised sources, nonconstant warping on a smooth compact space is possible. We derive their eleven-dimensional uplifts and four-dimensional Einstein-frame cosmology. Each universe undergoes (decelerating) expansion from a Big Bang, reaches a maximum size, and undergoes contraction towards a Big Crunch. We also analyse the scale separation of these backgrounds and find that they exhibit a small Einstein frame Hubble scale to KK mass ratio $\frac{|H_E|}{m_{\mathrm{KK}}}\ll1,$ although for a brief period of time, around the maxima of the scale factor in the Einstein frame. Finally, we analyse the supersymmetry of these backgrounds, which demonstrates that all three solutions break all forms of type IIA supersymmetry.

summary: We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench.For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

title: Optimal Search Strategies under Finite Resource Constraints: The Role of Environmental Memory and Directional Information in Informed and Blind Protocols
summary: Improving the efficiency of a stochastic search often requires to provide the searching agent with resources that modify its dynamics and help it explore space more quickly. Although such resources are often assumed to be unlimited and treated as a cost to mitigate, many realistic search processes operate under a finite resource budget, e.g. in processes with environmental memory in which the searcher deposits long-lasting cues along its path that it can interact with at later times to guide its further search. Here, we address the question of how to allocate a limited budget to maximize search efficiency by investigating a one-dimensional diffusing agent whose access to resources is constrained. We consider three resource models, namely an external force applied by an external controller to pull the searcher towards the target, directional flags deposited by the searcher along its path that redirect its motion towards the target, and self-generated chemorepulsive cues that act as a force field. For all these models, we find that resource usage should be concentrated in narrow regions of space when information about the searcher's current and past positions is available. In contrast, in blind strategies where a predefined time protocol is followed, resources should be used at a steady rate to ensure it to be used at most of its capacity by the time it reaches the target. We further show that blind strategies in non-Markovian processes with environmental memory are significantly less efficient due to the inherent fluctuations in the locations of deposited cues.

title: How good are universal MLIPs for alloys? A benchmark is only as trustworthy as its controls
comment: 47 pages (31 main + 16 SI), 12 figures; submitted to npj Computational Materials
summary: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are ranked by their formation-energy error against a DFT database, as if that database were ground truth, but independent DFT databases disagree. We benchmark fourteen uMLIPs on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, which none trained on, and compare every energy and stability error with that disagreement. For half the structures, AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD differ by less than 6-8 meV/atom, but a minority differ by far more, raising the average to 16-30. That disagreement sets a floor on any model's measurable error. Re-referenced, the best uMLIP agrees with AFLOW as closely as Alexandria does, and the next four sit 2-7 meV/atom above the floor. Once broken elemental references are screened, the energy and stability rankings agree almost everywhere. Three apparent model failures shrink or vanish under the right control: poorly correlated shear moduli, thousands of "bad" DFT references, and the leader's inflated lead.

title: Pressure in Wilsonian effective field theory
summary: We study the exponential rolling tachyon solution in Wilsonian effective field theory as a model for rolling tachyons in open string field theory. Although this solution exhibits runaway oscillations towards the future similar to its counterparts in string field theory, its pressure is shown to be consistent with the underlying bare theory, but only up to a finite time. The rest of the evolution of the pressure is instead governed by a solution that is oscillatory towards the past and regular at late times. We conjecture that the late time physics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by the solutions that are different from the standard rolling tachyon solutions based on this analysis.

title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
summary: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

title: Impact of localized $4f$ magnetism on Berry curvature and the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$
summary: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in $f$-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds. However, how the magnetism of localized $f$ electrons affect the intrinsic AHE remains unclear. Here, we investigate this issue in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$ by calculating the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) for several occupied Ce-$4f$ states using first-principles LDA+$U$ calculations combined with Wannier interpolation method. We find that the intrinsic AHC remains finite even when the Ce-$4f$ states are localized and do not contribute directly to the Fermi surface, and that its magnitude depends on which Ce-$4f$ state is occupied. We show that localized $4f$-electron magnetism induces exchange splitting in the conduction bands, generating Berry curvature in specific regions near the Fermi surface. This mechanism enables conduction bands that are derived from nonmagnetic orbitals and form the Fermi surface to contribute to the intrinsic AHE, suggesting a route to realizing large intrinsic AHE in $f$-electron materials.

title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

title: From phase analysis to phase tracking: a robust approach to atomic-scale strain mapping
summary: Atomic-scale strain governs the electronic, ferroic and mechanical properties of materials, and atomic-resolution microscopy measures it most directly. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) is the standard tool, but it fails when a Bragg reflection moves outside its fixed Fourier aperture under large strain or rotation, or in misoriented grains. Here we introduce geometric phase tracking analysis (GPTA), whose Fourier aperture tracks the Bragg reflection at each pixel in real space. A narrow aperture can therefore reject noise without losing a displaced reflection. On 13,795 simulated and experimental atomic-resolution images under various imaging conditions, GPTA reduces GPA's failure rate from 27% to 11.5% with up to 335 times better accuracy. It also gives strain and dislocation maps across grains, resistance to dynamical-scattering extinction, and a confidence map, capabilities that GPA lacks. Tracking the aperture combines reciprocal-space dose efficiency with real-space spatial resolution and extends atomic-scale strain metrology to beam-sensitive materials and challenging imaging conditions.

title: Fluids on null hypersurfaces and Carrollian hydrodynamics
summary: We study intrinsic ideal fluids on null hypersurfaces and their realisations by causal fluids living in the ambient spacetime. An embedded null hypersurface is equipped with an induced Carrollian structure with a temporal Weyl symmetry inherited from rescalings of the null generator, and we develop the corresponding null submanifold and variational calculus. The intrinsic fluid phases are classified according to their realisation of Carroll boosts and temporal Weyl symmetry. If we demand that an ambient fluid be confined to a null hypersurface, the ambient fluid velocity must be null, which realises an intrinsic zero-temperature Carrollian phase with unbroken Carroll boosts. In general, timelike or null ambient fluids will cross a null hypersurface and lead to an open Carrollian system. On a null foliation, the sources correspond to transport between null leaves. We then show that there exists a decoupling limit of a timelike ambient fluid which gives rise to an autonomous Carrollian fluid with spontaneously broken Carroll boosts and no source terms. This decoupling limit corresponds to an infinite boost while keeping the enthalpy finite and nonzero, which leads to a divergent ambient energy-momentum tensor. Nevertheless, the induced Carrollian responses do not see the divergent term and remain finite, and an independent Carroll boost Goldstone emerges from a subleading component of the ambient fluid velocity in this limit.

title: Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves
summary: We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.

title: Fit-error corrected auxiliary master equation approach for low-temperature nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory
summary: The auxiliary master equation approach (AMEA) is a nonperturbative impurity solver for steady-state nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). It replaces the physical hybridization function by that of a small auxiliary open quantum system, whose parameters are fitted to reproduce it, and then solves the resulting many-body problem essentially exactly. AMEA's accuracy is thus limited by the quality of this fit: since the fastest-varying part of the hybridization is set by the distribution function, whose Fermi edges sharpen at low temperature, the fit tends to overestimate the temperature, especially for weak reservoir coupling. For the auxiliary hybridization itself, however, AMEA's self-energy is essentially exact. We correct for the fit error by estimating, via an approximate solver applicable to arbitrary hybridization functions, the ratio between the self-energies of the physical and auxiliary hybridizations, and using it to extend AMEA's self-energy from the auxiliary to the physical case. This fit-error correction becomes exact whenever either the fit or the approximate solver is exact. We benchmark the scheme using the nonequilibrium Kajueter-Kotliar iterated perturbation theory (IPT), generalized here to spin-polarized solutions, as the approximate solver; other approximate solvers, such as the noncrossing approximation, can be used as well. Applied to an Anderson impurity model with a spin-polarized bath, and within DMFT to a Hubbard layer weakly coupled to two metallic reservoirs, the correction largely removes the spurious heating from the AMEA fit and from insufficient thermalization by the reservoirs, while preserving the correct description of the Mott insulator, which IPT alone cannot fully recover.

title: Discrete time liquids
comment: 8 pages main + 9 pages supplement, 4 figures main + 10 figures supplement
summary: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response.
